name: Vanguard fighter
role: The player's alien fighter (placeholder name). Flight numbers start on the GTF Ulysses'; the afterburner is the user's override (stronger than FS2's).

brakeDecel.source: USER REQUEST (design section 4, brake bullet, 2026-10-24: R3 brakes hard to a full stop with retro thrusters, much faster than the normal slow-down). Ours, the player's fighter only: 0.35 s against the slow-down's 1.5 s, so 70 m/s is below 3.5 m/s in 1.2 s (95 percent in 1.05 s) and stopped in about 1.7 s, a peak of 200 m/s^2 (20 g, the lurch the juice sells); from the 235 m/s burner it stops in under 2.2 s. FS2 has no brake: the four reference classes have none.

afterburner.source: Starting point: GTF Ulysses FS2 retail ships.tbl (Root_fs2.vp, sha256 60266906...315ca), field $Afterburner (brief: start our fighter on the Ulysses' numbers; tune from playtests)

afterburnerSpeed.source: USER OVERRIDE (design section 4, afterburner bullet, 2026-10-24: 'boosting feels weak ... needs to provide more speed for a really satisfying feeling'): the player's side gets 3.4 x its cruise speed on the burner (70 -> 235 m/s) instead of FS2's 2.1 x (GTF Ulysses +Aburn Max Vel (z) = 150, FS2 retail ships.tbl, Root_fs2.vp, sha256 60266906...315ca). Only the player's fighter class has it: the four FS2 reference classes keep FS2's numbers, so the flight model is still proven against FS2 (tools/flight.ps1, 35 of 35 on each). About 1.3 km covered in a full 6 s tank.

afterburnerAccel.source: USER OVERRIDE (same note): a punchier ramp than FS2's 0.7 s (GTF Ulysses +Aburn For accel): 63 % of the extra speed in 0.4 s (an initial push of about 410 m/s^2), 95 % in 1.2 s, so ignition is felt as a shove, not a drift. The juice (Monolith.Juice BoostFx) dresses it.
